elections.label: June 1954
elections.note: Chamber of Deputies, Kingdom of Iraq
elections.notes: Voting was delayed until 14 June in some areas; the date is the main polling day. Independents won the most seats (53) but no majority, so the Constitutional Union Party, the largest party (50) as the lead says, is flagged as the winner. "National Patriotic Front" links to the National Union Front article; its colour is the table's. The table gives seats only, no votes; changes are the table's ("New" stored as null). No turnout in the source. No results by governorate, so no region winners.

elections.note: National Assembly under Ba'ath Party rule
elections.notes: All candidates had been approved by a committee chaired by the Justice Minister, and the lead says 30 MPs were appointed to represent Iraqi Kurdistan; the table does not show them separately. The Kurdistan Democratic Party row links to the Kurdistan Democratic Party article, and the "Communist Party of Iraq" row to the Popular Unity Party (Iraq) article, whose keys are used. Turnout is the lead's 93.5% (the table's 7,480,000 votes of 8,000,000 registered). The table gives seats only, no votes; changes are the table's ("New" stored as null). No results by governorate, so no region winners.

elections.note: National Assembly under Ba'ath Party rule
elections.notes: The lead says all independents were nominally loyal to the Ba'ath Party. The 30 members for Sulaymaniyah, Erbil and Dohuk, where no election took place, were appointed by the government; the table lists them as a row. The table gives an electorate (9,200,000) but no votes cast, so no turnout is set. The table gives seats only, no votes; changes are the table's ("New" stored as null). No results by governorate, so no region winners.

elections.label: January 2005

source.name: Wikipedia, citing UNHCR and the Inter-Parliamentary Union

candidates.name: Islamic Action Organization In Iraq – Central Command

elections.notes: Elected the 275-member Transitional National Assembly. The lead says low Sunni Arab turnout (as low as 2% in Anbar) threatened its legitimacy. Shares are of the table's 8,456,263 votes for all lists; 94,305 invalid ballots are excluded. Others combines 72 lists under 1% without seats. The table has no change column. Turnout is computed from the table's electorate (14,662,639) and ballots cast; the article's text gives 58%. The linked results page has a by-governorate table only for Anbar, where the Iraqi List led (5,263 votes to 4,786); no other governorate has a winner.

elections.label: December 2005

candidates.name: Yazidi Movement for Reform and Progress

elections.notes: First election to the Council of Representatives under the new constitution. Sunni Arab and secular groups alleged fraud afterwards (not in the lead). Shares are of the table's 12,191,133 votes for all lists; 205,498 invalid ballots are excluded. Others combines the table's "Other parties" row (588,348 votes). Changes are the table's ("New" stored as null). Turnout is computed from the table's electorate (15,568,702) and ballots cast. The infobox map shows the leading list by governorate, but the article has no table, so no region winners.

source.name: Wikipedia, citing Psephos (Adam Carr's Election Archive)

elections.notes: The lead says there were numerous allegations of fraud and a Baghdad recount was ordered; the electoral commission found no sign of fraud. Shares are of the table's 11,526,412 votes for all lists. Others combines the table's "Others" row (572,183 votes). Changes are the table's. Turnout is the lead's 62.4% (the table gives the electorate but not the ballots cast). Region winners are the list with the most seats in each governorate in the article's by-governorate seat table (it has no votes); its "al-Iraqiya" column is the Iraqi National Movement. Kirkuk is a tie and is left out. That table's source link is dead.

source.name: Wikipedia, citing ORSAM (from the Independent High Electoral Commission results)

candidates.name: Unity of the Sons of Iraq
Yazidi Movement for Reform and Progress

elections.notes: The Al-Ahrar Bloc was the Sadrists' list; it links to the Sadrist movement's article (National Shiite Movement), as the 2021 Sadrist Movement does, so they share a key. "Kurdistan Islamic Group" links to the Kurdistan Justice Group (its later name). The State of Law Coalition's change is given as "3" (taken as +3). Shares are of the table's 13,013,765 votes for all lists. Others combines the table's "Other parties" row (1,782,452 votes). Changes are the table's ("New" or blank stored as null). Turnout is the infobox's 62% (the table gives the electorate but not the ballots cast). Region winners are the list with the most votes in each governorate's table in the article, leaving out its "Other" rows. The Anbar, Erbil, Babil, Baghdad, Basra and Dhi Qar tables repeat one figure for every zero-seat list (apparently the other lists' combined total); the leading list has more votes than that figure in each, so the winners are unaffected.

source.name: Wikipedia, citing the Independent High Electoral Commission

candidates.name: Assembly of the Men of Iraq

elections.notes: The lead says parliament ordered a manual recount in June 2018 and that a storage site holding about half the ballots caught fire; the results section describes claims of widespread fraud linked to electronic counting. Seats include minority quota seats won by lists such as the Babylon Movement and the Rafidain List. Shares are of the table's 10,374,533 votes for all lists. Others combines 34 lists under 1% without seats. The table has no change column. No turnout: the article gives none, and the table gives the electorate but not the ballots cast. Region winners are the list with the most votes in each governorate's table in the article.

source.name: Wikipedia, citing the Independent High Electoral Commission

elections.notes: First election under the single non-transferable vote in 83 districts. The lead says the results led to protests and an 11-month political crisis. "Independent" (1,686,792 votes, 43 seats) is the table's total for independent candidates. Shares are of the table's 8,854,025 votes for all lists (the table's valid-vote figure is 8,906,959); 722,642 invalid ballots are excluded. Others combines 95 lists under 1% without seats. The table has no change column. Turnout is computed from the table's valid and invalid votes and electorate (22,116,368); the infobox gives 43.30%. The article gives results by district (83 districts), not by governorate, so no region winners.
